novella.title: Hic Non Sunt Dracones
novella.tagline: London, 1897. The age of exploration is dying.
description: In the decadent halls of the St. James Society, clerks replace explorers. Discovery is measured in profit. But Major Jason Havelock—a veteran of debatable exploits and absolute conviction—refuses to live in a world without wonder.
When the Society's last expedition is cancelled, Havelock produces a forgotten map. It hints at a lost city deep in the Brazilian wilderness. His plan is simple. Reality couldn't be further from it.

The entrance to that lost city lies at the heart of the War of Canudos—a brutal civil war that has been raging for almost a year. After three disastrous expeditions, the Brazilian Army is preparing to level the rebel stronghold once and for all. Havelock's crew? A disgraced, trigger-happy lieutenant. A scarred mining engineer. A young clerk who has never left London.
To reach their objective, these misfits must cross a battlefield, evade blockades and ambushes, and survive a climate that seems at war with everyone.
At the dawn of industrial warfare, one old soldier is chasing a whisper from the blank spaces of our maps.
<strong>The last charge of the light brigade is about to begin.
Not a prequel. Not a sequel. Just a story. My own take on classical adventure, and an invitation to think about what comes next.
